title: Python SDK: Typed response models and structured-output helper utilities
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Customers want first-class typed parsing of model outputs in the Python SDK so application code can rely on structured data rather than brittle string parsing. The SDK currently has ad-hoc helpers; we need a unified, ergonomic layer that supports both pydantic and dataclasses, integrates with streaming responses, and plays nicely with retry/partial-result semantics.

Goal: Implement a set of typed model helpers and structured-output convenience functions that: produce typed objects from full or partial responses, validate and surface schema errors clearly, and expose streaming-friendly parsers that can produce incremental typed outputs for UI consumption. Ensure backwards compatibility with existing helper functions and provide clear migration docs and examples.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New helpers exist: TypedModelBase (pydantic-compatible), dataclass_adapter, parse_response_to_model(response, model_class), stream_parse_to_model(stream_iterator, model_class).
2) Helpers validate outputs; validation errors include source token offsets and raw text.
3) Streaming parser emits partial typed objects as soon as a valid JSON chunk can be constructed and validated.
4) Unit and integration tests cover sync/async, retries (idempotent vs non-idempotent), and edge cases (truncated JSON, invalid types).
5) Documentation examples for pydantic and dataclasses and a migration guide from old helpers.
6) No performance regression (>5% token-level throughput) in standard bench harness for common workloads.
implementation_notes:
Design decisions:
- Provide a thin TypedModelBase that wraps pydantic BaseModel when pydantic is installed, otherwise falls back to a minimal dataclass validator. Keep runtime dependency optional.
- Expose two primary APIs: parse_response_to_model(response_text: str, model: Type) -> instance and async stream_parse_to_model(async_iterator[str], model: Type) -> AsyncIterator[PartialResult].
- PartialResult is a flattened string + optional validated_model field and an errors list. We will represent PartialResult as a simple typed tuple-like dataclass for users.
- For streaming, implement a resilient incremental JSON accumulator that tolerates trailing commas and concatenated JSON objects from models. Use a safe JSON extraction heuristics: balance-based chunking with fallback to regex-based last-brace extraction.
- Retries: parsing should be idempotent; the retry layer will retry raw generation requests, and parsers must dedupe duplicate partials if upstream replays tokens. We'll expose a simple token_sequence_id annotation for clients to handle deduplication if needed.
- Backcompat: wrap old helpers path in the new module with deprecation warnings for one release.
- Performance: implement C-optimized JSON scanning is out of scope; prefer micro-optimized Python logic and benchmark.

API sketch (example):

class TypedModelBase:
    """Base wrapper that prefers pydantic if available, otherwise dataclass style validation."""

    def validate(cls, raw: dict) -> object: ...

# Synchronous usage
from redwood_sdk.structured_output import parse_response_to_model
from examples.models import OrderPrediction

raw = response.get_text()
order = parse_response_to_model(raw, OrderPrediction)  # raises ValidationError with source snippets on error

# Streaming usage (async)
async for partial in stream_parse_to_model(response.aiter_text(), OrderPrediction):
    if partial.validated_model is not None:
        render_ui(partial.validated_model)
    elif partial.errors:
        log(parital.errors)
api_examples:
Example (pydantic):

from pydantic import BaseModel
from redwood_sdk.structured_output import parse_response_to_model

class Customer(BaseModel):
    id: str
    name: str
    loyalty_tier: str | None = None

resp_text = '{"id":"c_123","name":"Dana","loyalty_tier":"gold"}'
customer = parse_response_to_model(resp_text, Customer)

# Example (dataclass):
from dataclasses import dataclass
from redwood_sdk.structured_output import dataclass_adapter, parse_response_to_model

@dataclass
class Item:
    sku: str
    qty: int

ItemAdapter = dataclass_adapter(Item)
parsed = parse_response_to_model('{"sku":"X-99","qty":2}', ItemAdapter)

# Streaming example (pseudo):
async for partial in stream_parse_to_model(aiostream, OrderPrediction):
    # partial.text contains accumulated raw text; partial.validated_model is populated when validation passes
    if partial.validated_model:
        print('Validated:', partial.validated_model)
migration_notes:
- Old helpers located at redwood_sdk.helpers.structured_output are deprecated; import paths will still work but emit DeprecationWarning.
- New API lives under redwood_sdk.structured_output; prefer parse_response_to_model and stream_parse_to_model.
- If you relied on raw token slices for error reporting, switch to PartialResult.raw_snippets which maps model validation errors to source substrings.
- If you used custom JSON extraction, consider using the new incremental_json_accumulator helper instead of ad-hoc regex logic.
testing_plan:
Unit tests: validate success and failure cases for both pydantic and dataclass flows, including nested models and optional fields.
Integration tests: run against local mock LLM that emits JSON-incremental streams, simulate truncated streams and duplicated token sequences.
Performance tests: run existing token-throughput harness to measure before/after (target <5% regression).
Fuzz tests: random text + valid JSON fragments to ensure parser is robust.
CI: Add matrix for with-pydantic and without-pydantic environments.
Acceptance runbook: checklist to validate release candidate against the acceptance_criteria above.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature behind feature flag 'typed-output-v2'. 2) Roll out to internal customers and SDK beta testers. 3) Monitor error rates and validation exceptions in console (new telemetry: structured_output.validation.errors). 4) After 2 weeks stable, flip default to enabled and publish migration guide. 5) Deprecate old helper imports in next minor release with clear upgrade notes.
